attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post. The Bloomberg quote covers only the phrase 'day and night'.

semantics.note: The draft keeps both examples and the oil antecedent. 'Will become' is firm language, so this is a scoreable conditional forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'extra-normally' as well above normal year-on-year moves is an ordinary reading. Treating the two examples as one forecast, with freight as the measurable one, is fair because Abilene mobilization cost has no public measure.

evidence.note: EIA: Brent peaked in April 2026, after the post. This shows the antecedent was met, not the outcome.
TAC: jet fuel rose steeply in March and April 2026. This is evidence of the condition and the cost driver.
The global BAI00 index was about 33% above a year earlier, above usual peak-season levels. It is a global index, not lane-specific.
TAC data show very significant year-on-year gains for Taiwan to US, but give no figures. Part of the rise is linked to AI-driven demand.

reviews.rationale: Oil and jet fuel kept rising after the post (peak in April). By 1 June the TAC/Baltic index showed air freight about a third above year-earlier levels, at peak-season-like levels, with large Taiwan-to-US gains. That meets the early-resolution rule for the freight example. The Abilene part cannot be measured, and some of the freight rise came from AI demand rather than fuel alone.

attribution.note: Zitron describes the affidavit in his own words and asserts the intent himself. The figures come from Rao's declaration, but the characterization and the deception claim are his.

semantics.note: The draft captures the $5B lifetime revenue, the $10B spend and the intent allegation. 'About $5 billion' softens his 'is $5 billion' slightly, which is acceptable.

contract.note: It is fair to require evidence of intent beyond a numerical mismatch, and to keep the declaration's lower-bound wording. The approximate-total reading follows his own $5.5B ceiling argument.

evidence.note: Paragraph 8 of the declaration says revenue exceeded $5B and spend was over $10B. These are lower bounds. It gives no total or ceiling and no evidence of intent. The quoted line is from the right paragraph.

reviews.rationale: The declaration gives only lower bounds ('exceeding $5 billion', 'over $10 billion'). It does not establish an approximate $5B total. Nothing in the packet shows knowingly misleading revenue messaging, and nothing disproves it. The packet cannot settle either the totals or the intent.

attribution.note: Zitron's own firm assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Not a chance in Hell' is an unhedged, certain statement about 2025 revenue. 'Based on its CFO's affidavit' is his reasoning, not a condition, so dropping it does not change the claim.

contract.note: The plain reading (calendar 2025 realized revenue below $4.5B) is fair. The extra rule excluding GAAP is stretched: audited S-1 revenue is itself company-reported realized revenue for 2025, so it meets the contract's own contradiction condition.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, filed before the evaluation date, reports audited 2025 revenue of $4,585M. That is company-reported realized revenue for calendar 2025, at or above $4.5B.

reviews.rationale: He said with certainty that Anthropic did not make $4.5B in 2025. The company's own audited S-1 reports $4.585B for calendar 2025. GAAP revenue the company itself reports is company-reported, so the basis distinction does not make it non-comparable. The contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Is going to get much more expensive' is a firm forecast. The link to the gas price spike comes from the next sentence of the post.

contract.note: Henry Hub is a fair measure because he cited higher US consumer prices. With no deadline, judging the six-plus months after the post is reasonable given his framing of the current spike.

evidence.note: Gives the 2025 Henry Hub average of $3.53. The $3.09 Feb–Dec 2026 average includes forecast months, so it is used as context.
Actual monthly Henry Hub prices were $2.77–$3.15 from March to September 2026. All are below February ($3.62) and below the 2025 average.
EIA explains that ample storage held prices down.

reviews.rationale: Henry Hub monthly averages stayed below the February 2026 level and the 2025 average in every month from March to September 2026. That meets the early-resolution rule. US turbine fuel got cheaper after the post, not much more expensive.
